label: About
title: About Sky Lying in the Leaves
short_blurb: A daily generated front page where the image is the interface.
body: Daily Frontpage is a daily generated interactive front page. Each edition starts from a saved source, becomes a new image-led scene, and stays explorable in the archive. The image is the interface: a visible mark in the scene opens the real source that shaped the day.

This edition began with one saved post, @archaeologyart: Shirō Kasamatsu - Into the Woods, (1955). Its image from pbs.twimg.com set the palette, contrast, edge behavior, and gesture. The scene became Sky Lying in the Leaves: Woodblock forest floor seen from a low standing tilt, wide landscape plate, horizontal meander composition, high horizon of dark trunks cropped at the top edge. A long sky-blue pool aperture meanders across the lower middle like a cut-out river, holding indigo trunk reflections and rose branch filaments; one slender... After the image was made, a plate-reading pass mapped the source to Scalloped sky-reflecting puddle with inverted trunks in the leaf floor.

typography.rationale: Bricolage Grotesque and Space Grotesk fit record, arcade, and listening-room editions while Fraunces keeps source captions tactile.
